headline: Portable genomics software targets verifiable equivalence across languages and platforms
label: Reproducible Bioinformatics Tool Infrastructure
summary: Recent preprints and one published library report cross-language implementations, exchange formats and in-place analysis of large atlases.
synthesis: The dominant thread is portability of analysis software across languages, data formats and execution environments. BiocPy mirrors Bioconductor genomic data structures as Python packages, with lossless R (.rds) and ArtifactDB exchange and shared C++ methods across R and Python. The St. Nicolas House Analysis case study transpiles one Fusion implementation into nine languages and reports identical outputs across them. CyteArc addresses a related concern from the data side, analyzing remote single-cell atlases of about 100 million cells in place with provenance tracking and minimal disk use. SingloCell and snputils are less directly about reproducibility, providing a browser-based multimodal exploration platform and a Python library for biobank-scale population genetics, respectively. What is new is the explicit focus on verifiable equivalence across implementations and execution environments, which is reported directly only in the transpilation study.
